verses.title: Qualities of Amalaki fruit
verses.devanagari:
अम्लं समधुरं तिक्तं कषायं कटुकं सरम् ।
चक्षुष्यं सर्वदोषघ्नं वृष्यमामलकीफलम् ॥ १४३ ॥
verses.iast:
amlaṃ samadhuraṃ tiktaṃ kaṣāyaṃ kaṭukaṃ saram |
cakṣuṣyaṃ sarvadoṣaghnaṃ vṛṣyam āmalakīphalam || 143 ||
verses.translation: The Amalaki fruit is described as sour, sweet, bitter, astringent and pungent, with a moving (sara) property; traditionally considered beneficial for the eyes, countering the doṣas, and vṛṣya.
verses.editorial_note: Word segmentation and translation are study drafts. The passage concerns Amalaki fruit specifically.
word_by_word: said to counter all three doṣas

verses.title: Why the fruit is described as tridoṣajit
verses.devanagari:
हन्ति वातं तदम्लत्वात्पित्तं माधुर्यशैत्यतः ।
कफं रूक्षकषायत्वात्फलं धात्र्यास्त्रिदोषजित् ॥ ४० ॥
verses.iast:
hanti vātaṃ tad amlatvāt pittaṃ mādhuryaśaityataḥ |
kaphaṃ rūkṣakaṣāyatvāt phalaṃ dhātryās tridoṣajit || 40 ||
verses.translation: The fruit is described as countering Vāta due to sourness, Pitta due to sweetness and coolness, and Kapha due to dryness and astringency; thus the fruit of Dhātrī is called tridoṣajit.
verses.editorial_note: Electronic verse numbering varies: the NIIMH-derived index groups Āmalakī at 36–38; SanskritDocuments numbers this as 40. Do not merge verse IDs without a source edition.
word_by_word: one that overcomes the three doṣas

verses.title: Taste, cooling nature, and classical actions
verses.devanagari:
आमलकं कषायाम्लं मधुरं शिशिरं लघु ।
दाहपित्तवमीमेहशोफघ्नं च रसायनम् ॥
verses.iast:
āmalakaṃ kaṣāyāmlaṃ madhuraṃ śiśiraṃ laghu |
dāha-pitta-vamī-meha-śopha-ghnaṃ ca rasāyanam ||
verses.translation: The text describes Amalaki as astringent-sour, sweet, cooling and light; traditionally credited with countering burning, Pitta, vomiting, meha and swelling, and termed rasāyana.
verses.editorial_note: Source is an electronic transcription/interpretive index; collate against a printed Rāja Nighaṇṭu edition before approving lexical sandhi splits.
